items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: Was Brookmeyer in that? I think Brookmeyer was part — it was either Brookmeyer or Rob McConnell.

ctx.x: interpretations. But even for what I do, and I learned very early on of having to put different bands together and create different things. You can’t just usually put a band together and hope that — and say, “Okay we want you to play — we want you to do a tribute to Jazz at the Philharmonic and we want you to do a Jazz at the Philharmonic type concert” because there’ll be a lot of standing around and either one of two things will happen. Either one person that’s a Gerry Mulligan type will just step forward and…

respect from the musicians that they would really, really buckle down when they were doing the rehearsals to show the respect. Sometimes not. Sometimes you would run into problems. But a guy like Gerry, that was never a problem. A guy like Marty Paich was never a problem, because they’re going to get up there, and Gerry didn’t care who it was. When we did those “Rebirth of the Cool” things we did a rehearsal before one of the concerts, that would have been in L.A. at A&M. Herb Alpert would let us use A&M…
Do you have a place that you wish you could have been, to get in a time machine and experience a particular recording, a particular event?
